newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Max to raise more cash to fund purchase.
newsitem.headline: Max to raise more cash to fund purchase.

text.p: New Zealand-listed Max Resources said on Thursday it would raise equity to pay for the purchase of technology which converts chicken waste to organic fertiliser.
Max has conditionally agreed to buy a half share in PT WRS Indonesia, a company which has constructed a plant in Jakarta capable of producing 50,000 tonnes of organic fertiliser annually.
The plant is expected to be in full commercial production by March 1997. PT WRS Indonesia is budgeting profit before tax of approximately NZ$100 per tonne on achieving full production.
The total project cost upon commissioning will be approx. US$5 million with US$3.7 million from bank loans.

Max is also buying a 50 percent shareholding in Waste Recovery Systems (India) Ltd; a company which is constructing a plant in Hyderabad capable of producing 50,000 tonnes of rated organic fertiliser per annum.
Max expects this plant to be completed by the end of the year.
The other half owner in this company is Adytha Group Ltd.
The total cost of building the plant is U$4 million with US$3.250 milllion in borrowings in place from a syndicate of local and international banks.
Once again Max expects a profit before tax of NZ$100 per tonne once full production has been reached.

Max has also agreed to buy half of a shareholding in WRS Sri Lanka, a 50/50 joint venture interest with the Sri Lankian Tea Board. This venture has the aim of building a plant in Colombo capable of producing 50,000 tonnes of rated organic fertiliser per annum.
Max has also acquired ownership of certain intellectual property related to the technology which converts raw chicken waste into a rated organic fertiliser completely free of pathogens.

The acquisitions relate to a change in the essential nature of Max's business and a meeting of shareholders to approve the transactions and the change in business will be called as soon as NZ Stock Exchange approval of meeting documents is received.
The company said a meeting will be held next month.
